outcome: Depth of anesthesia (measured by Bispectral Index Monitoring - BIS values)
Hemodynamic changes (Systolic Blood Pressure - SBP, Diastolic Blood Pressure - DBP, Mean Arterial Pressure - MBP, Heart Rate - HR, Oxygen Saturation - SpO2)
cohort: The study included 72 pregnant individuals undergoing general anesthesia for cesarean section, divided into two groups: those receiving preoperative MgSO4 and controls.
finding: Preoperative administration of MgSO4 significantly provided a more stable and deeper level of anesthesia during general anesthesia for cesarean sections, as indicated by BIS values, compared to controls, without significant differences in demographic or most hemodynamic parameters.
